tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (agent won't start, gateway fails, returns nothing, behaves differently in prod) rather than internals, explicitly lists trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name the domain directly ('even if they do not mention runtime roles, VPC endpoints...'), and remains a concise paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when an agent will not start, cannot be invoked or cannot call its model, when a gateway or action group fails, when an agent returns nothing, when it behaves differently in production than in test, or when someone asks which agent version is actually live, even if they do not mention runtime roles, VPC endpoints, service control policies or aliasing by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense with domain-specific, non-obvious facts (maintenance-mode nuances, SCP interactions, session policy intersection rules, AgentCore namespace gaps) rather than explaining general concepts the agent already knows. No filler explaining basic AWS or agent concepts was found.
tests.evidence: "Classic is in maintenance mode: per the Agents Classic maintenance mode page it is no longer open to new customers from July 30, 2026..."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body delegates detailed check catalogs, API quirks, and metric thresholds to references/ files rather than embedding large tables or lookup data inline. The router table is concise pointers, not full reference content.
tests.evidence: "Every finding is grounded in the catalogs under `references/`: `checks-agentcore.md` (LLM-AC-001..014...) and `checks-agents.md` (LLM-AGT-001..011...)"

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All files in references/ are linked via markdown links in the body (collection-reference.md, checks-agentcore.md, checks-agents.md, api-quirks.md, router-details.md, runtime-sessions.md, metrics-and-logs.md, related-skills.md).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: References are tied to specific conditions in the router table and procedure steps, specifying when to load each file (e.g., tied to specific symptoms or steps).

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root in the format references/filename.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (permission checks, SCP evaluation, alias resolution) get exact prescriptive steps, while softer judgment areas (hypothesis labeling, scope disclosure) are explained with reasoning rather than rigid scripts, matching specificity to fragility.
tests.evidence: "Never call `iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy`... read the role's inline and attached policies... and check each required action against them"

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple paths exist (e.g., migration options), a default/primary path is clearly indicated (AgentCore over Classic) with alternatives noted as options, not presented as an undifferentiated menu.
tests.evidence: "recommend migrating via the **AgentCore harness** (config-based, closest analog) or **code-defined agents on AgentCore**"

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The procedures teach generalizable diagnostic approaches (e.g., check runtime role permissions, resolve alias to version, check VPC endpoints) that apply to any instance of the respective failure type, not one-off declarations.
